title: I was supposed to draw a little pixel art car... somehow I'm developing an entire app now 💀
author: KaleidoscopeMany9272
selftext:
Okay so I'm getting pretty close to finishing **ROAD RADIO**, and I genuinely can't believe this whole thing started with a random conversation with a friend lmao.

Basically, my friend challenged me to draw an isometric room in Aseprite. Normal stuff, right? Well, for some reason my brain went "what if I draw a car instead?" and that's exactly what I did.

Around that time I was messing around with this little Steam app called Mini Cozy Room (really cute app btw), and while looking at my car I randomly told my friend, "BRO WHAT IF I MAKE A LITTLE DESKTOP PET BUT FOR CAR PEOPLE??"

And apparently that was enough motivation for me to start developing an entire piece of software. 💀

I actually posted the original pixel art car here on Reddit, and some dude commented something along the lines of "why don't you just make a 3D model and render it as pixel art?"

And I was like... wait. Bro kinda has a point.

So I tried it. And then I kept adding stuff. And changing stuff. And adding more stuff. You know how it goes when you have absolutely zero self-control over your own projects 😭

At some point I hit this weird creative wall where I genuinely had no idea what direction to take anymore. So I started watching an unhealthy amount of software development videos, game dev videos, reading about design, looking at other people's projects, basically trying to find inspiration ANYWHERE.

I even went back to playing old N64 games and a bunch of indie games. Which sounds completely unrelated because, well, I'm making software, not a game. But I figured good ideas don't necessarily have to come from the same medium, right?

Then I started playing Borderlands 2 again.

And oh boy.

That kinda changed everything for me visually. I started experimenting with a more stylized, cel-shaded look, with those bold outlines and illustrated shadows. Eventually I decided to move away from the original pixel art direction entirely.

Which is funny because pixel art was literally the reason this project existed in the first place.

Also, since I know people are curious about AI in development, yes, I've used AI while making this. Mostly to help clean up and refactor code I'd already written, catch things I overlooked, and bounce ideas around when my brain decided to clock out for the day lol.

I've written most of the code myself, and I've been learning a TON throughout the process. I don't really see AI as something that should replace the creative part for me. I actually enjoy figuring things out, experimenting, and occasionally making terrible decisions that take me three hours to fix.

That's like half the fun of being a developer anyway. (The other half is wondering why something that worked yesterday suddenly doesn't work today.)

Anyway, I just wanted to share how this weird little project evolved because I genuinely wasn't expecting to get this attached to it.

It's been a lot of experimenting, redesigning, breaking things, fixing them, and questioning my life choices.

But I'm really happy with where it's going.

**So yeah, here's ROAD RADIO!!** 🚗📻

I'd genuinely love to hear what you guys think about the new art direction, especially compared to the original pixel art version.

And if you've ever started a tiny project that somehow spiraled into something WAY bigger than you planned... please tell me I'm not the only one. 😭
